evidence.claim: Kroger's FY2024 10-K described its retail business as generating traffic and data that support high-margin alternative-profit businesses including Kroger Precision Marketing, data analytics services, and third-party media revenue.
evidence.source_title: The Kroger Co. Form 10-K filed April 1, 2025

evidence.claim: Kroger's 2025 Responsible Business Report stated that the company manufactures 31% of total Our Brands products and stocks over 12,000 private-label items.

Symbotic's investor-relations site lists its Second Quarter Fiscal Year 2026 results and related Form 10-Q materials, confirming an active latest-filing source for automation deployment and customer-concentration checks.

Cal-Maine reported fiscal 2025 average customer selling price of $3.134 per dozen versus $1.932 in fiscal 2024, with higher market prices primarily tied to reduced industry shell-egg supply from HPAI.

Cal-Maine's FY2025 annual report states that shell eggs have approximately 97% household penetration and that U.S. eggs are heavily sold through food-at-home outlets such as grocery and convenience channels.
Fair Isaac's FY2025 annual report noted that business-to-business Scores revenue increased due to higher unit price, increased mortgage-origination volume, and a U.S. insurance-score license renewal.
evidence.source_title: Fair Isaac Corporation Form 10-K filed November 7, 2025

evidence.claim: Equifax FY2025 10-K materials described Workforce Solutions revenue growth driven by Verification Services and cited strong growth in consumer-lending-related diversified markets.
Capital One reported fourth-quarter 2025 net income of $2.1 billion and disclosed year-ended 2025 credit-card net charge-offs in its earnings materials.
evidence.source_title: Capital One Reports Fourth Quarter 2025 Net Income

evidence.claim: Capital One's 2025 annual report includes credit-card and consumer-banking credit metrics, including net charge-off amounts and rates by portfolio.
Affirm's FY2025 impact report stated that the company served about 23 million active consumers, generated $36.7 billion of FY2025 GMV, and had 95% of transactions from repeat users.
Affirm's FY2025 annual report identifies GMV, transaction frequency, active consumers, average order value, Affirm Card activity, and virtual debit-card activity as operating drivers.
Instacart stated that it partners with more than 2,200 retail banners representing nearly 100,000 stores and operates Marketplace, Enterprise platform, and Ads ecosystem offerings.
evidence.source_title: Instacart Announces Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2025 Financial Results

evidence.claim: Instacart's May 2026 Form 8-K materials showed Q1 2026 GTV of $10.288 billion, total revenue of $1.019 billion, and adjusted EBITDA of $300 million.

Tractor Supply reported Q2 2025 comparable sales growth driven by year-round categories, especially consumable, usable and edible products, plus spring seasonal demand, partly offset by softer discretionary categories.
evidence.source_title: Tractor Supply Company Reports Second Quarter 2025 Financial Results

evidence.claim: Tractor Supply's FY2025 annual materials referenced opening 99 new stores, growing Neighbor's Club, and investing in direct sales, pet and animal Rx, and final-mile delivery initiatives.
evidence.source_title: Tractor Supply 2025 Annual Report and 2026 Proxy Statement

evidence.claim: Etsy's FY2025 10-K reported that Etsy marketplace GMS declined 4% in 2025 to $10.5 billion and cited ongoing pressure on consumer discretionary spending and evolving buyer behavior.
Etsy reported FY2025 revenue of $2.884 billion and Q4 2025 adjusted EBITDA margin of 25.2%, while noting slight Etsy marketplace GMS growth in Q4.
evidence.source_title: Etsy Reports Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2025 Results

evidence.claim: eBay's FY2025 10-K materials reported Q4 2025 GMV of $21.2 billion, up 10% as reported and 8% FX-neutral, and emphasized momentum in recommerce.
eBay's Q4 2025/FY2025 materials stated that focus category GMV grew more than 12% year over year in 2025, driven by collectibles, parts and accessories, and fashion.
evidence.source_title: eBay Q4 2025 and FY2025 Earnings Deck

evidence.claim: Whirlpool's 2025 annual report stated that the company reported approximately $16 billion in annual net sales, with close to 90% in the Americas.

Whirlpool's 2025 annual report described a challenging macroeconomic environment, a shifting tariff landscape, pressure from Asian competitors' pre-tariff stockpiles, and expectations tied to an overdue housing recovery.

memory_update.text: KR should be retained as a grocery/private-label/retail-media Consumer candidate; evidence quality is good but needs FY2025 extraction for identical sales, digital sales, and alternative-profit contribution.
CALM is a strong regulated perishable-staples node with explicit HPAI and shell-egg pricing sensitivity; it should be tracked as a supply-chain constraint rather than a simple consumer-demand ticker.
CART is one of the cleaner grocery ecommerce and retail-media mappings in the chunk because company evidence directly connects Marketplace, Enterprise, Ads, GTV, orders, and retailer partnerships.
TSCO maps to rural specialty retail with recurring consumables and pet/livestock exposure; tariff and discretionary-category softness should be monitored as falsifiers.
ETSY should be tagged as discretionary-risk ecommerce rather than value/staples; FY2025 GMS weakness is a key negative evidence point despite revenue resilience.
EBAY's Consumer mapping is strongest through recommerce/value-seeking and focus categories, not broad ecommerce beta.
WHR is a lower-priority Consumer candidate until housing turnover, tariff mitigation, and North America margin recovery evidence improves.
AFRM belongs in the consumer-credit/ecommerce-conversion node; it requires continuous loss, funding, and repeat-user monitoring because the relationship can invert under consumer stress.
COF is a credit-cycle and payments-volume mapping rather than a pure consumer-spending beneficiary; charge-offs and funding costs are the key chokepoint evidence.
SYM needs direct latest 10-Q extraction for customer concentration, backlog quality, deployment timing, and Walmart-related exposure before it can be ranked against direct Consumer demand nodes.
FICO and EFX need normalized segment-level evidence separating mortgage-cycle exposure from durable underwriting/data-rail demand.
All tickers in this chunk still need Layer 2C market-pricing checks: valuation, earnings revisions, price reaction to latest earnings, short interest, and consensus growth expectations.

summary: Mapped the candidate Consumer chunk into ticker-to-node relationships across grocery/private-label/retail media, fulfillment automation, regulated food inputs, consumer-credit data rails, consumer credit balance sheets, BNPL/ecommerce credit, grocery delivery platforms, specialty consumables retail, discretionary marketplaces, recommerce, and housing-linked durables. Highest-quality relationships in this pass are KR, CALM, CART, TSCO, ETSY, EBAY, WHR, AFRM and COF because recent company filings/releases directly tie them to the relevant consumer nodes. SYM, FICO and EFX remain plausible infrastructure mappings but need tighter latest-filing extraction for customer concentration, segment economics, and credit-cycle sensitivity.
